coverage: 120-case development slice (15 held-out tasks, 8 editors) + 232 official training cases

usage.note: A first run made 176 warm-start judge calls before failing on a missing textgrad==0.1.8 install; those were reused via --checkpoint-from and not repaid.

metric_3_evidence_referral.finding: The three target-blind evidence signals fire too rarely on this data to produce a useful referral: three-way consensus ties occur in ~0.6% of training cases and none were disputed; the routed node's similarity clears its threshold so low_route_similarity never triggers; and unsupported_route at support>=1 never triggers. Under the 0.5 coverage floor the fit degenerates to zero abstention. This is a genuine negative result for the current evidence-signal design, not a pipeline error.

comparison_editor_reliability_selective_.note: The existing consensus + editor-reliability selective_policy remains the stronger referral for this dataset; evidence_policy as defined does not beat it here.

tree_metrics.root_coverage_note: Reported root_coverage is relative to leaf-assigned (fit) cases and can exceed 1 when the global root also covers held-in validation cases; it is a diagnostic, not a bounded fraction.

conclusion: The measurement suite (ordinal MAE, consensus-referral precision/recall/F1, tree-compression + routing metrics) and the evidence_policy wiring run correctly end-to-end on live gpt-4.1-mini. On this development slice the evidence-based referral does not fire and does not improve on the editor-reliability selective policy; richer or more frequently-firing target-blind signals (e.g., consensus support bands, a partial-specific evidence field, or a lower similarity margin) are the next thing to try. Cali-Tree v2 full-coverage accuracy and the reserved untouched partitions are unaffected.
